scenelets.scene: Declining street vendors or aggressive sales
scenelets.notes: 'No gracias' alone with eye contact and a slight smile is sufficient and respected. Avoid elaborate explanations — they invite further pitch.

phrases.es: Qué amable, pero hoy no puedo.
phrases.en: How kind, but I can't today.
I'd love to, but I have plans.
I don't drink alcohol, thank you.

phrases.es: Qué rico se ve, pero ya no puedo más.
phrases.en: It looks delicious, but I really can't eat more.

scenelets.notes: In Mexican hospitality culture, refusing food can feel like a slight. Acknowledge the food warmly before declining.

phrase_cards.notes: The full stop of refusal — complete and gracious

phrase_cards.en: I have a commitment / prior engagement

phrase_cards.notes: Soft, warm close to any refusal

register_map.cultural_note: Mexicans generally don't take 'no' as cold — they take abruptness as cold. Warm the refusal with a word of appreciation first.
register_map.warmth_move: Lead with a compliment: 'qué amable' or 'qué generoso' before the refusal lands.
